subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Cars and Climate Change
description: A quick win: understand Cars and Climate Change.

hook.text: Transportation produces about a quarter of global CO2 emissions, and passenger cars are the largest chunk.

buildup.text: Switching all cars to electric would slash emissions—but only if the electricity itself comes from clean sources.

discovery.text: Manufacturing an EV battery produces significant CO2, meaning new EVs start life with a carbon debt to repay.

twist.text: That debt is usually repaid within 1 to 3 years of driving, after which the EV is cleaner mile for mile.

climax.text: Electrification alone won't solve the climate crisis—fewer cars, shorter trips, and cleaner grids must all combine.

punchline.text: Electric cars help, but they're one piece of a much larger puzzle.

quiz.question: How long does it typically take for an EV to offset its manufacturing carbon debt?

details.summary: Road transport accounts for roughly 16 percent of global CO2 emissions, making the shift to zero-emission vehicles one of the most critical steps in fighting climate change.
details.whyItMatters: With over 1.4 billion cars on the road, even small efficiency gains have massive impact. Electrification and cleaner fuels are essential to meeting global climate targets.
takeaways: Transport produces about 16 percent of global CO2 emissions
EVs can cut per-car emissions by 50 to 70 percent over their lifetime
The pace of fleet turnover limits how fast emissions fall

faq.question: Are electric cars really better for the climate given battery manufacturing?
faq.answer: Yes. Even accounting for mining and manufacturing, EVs produce significantly fewer lifetime emissions than gasoline cars, especially where the electricity grid uses renewable energy.

faq.question: How long will it take for the entire car fleet to go electric?
faq.answer: The average car stays on the road for 12 to 15 years. Even with strong EV sales, full fleet turnover will likely take until the 2040s or 2050s in most countries.
